WBCQ's 500 kW Superstation Is Up for Lease: What It Means for 9330 kHz

By Michael Smith · October 12, 2026 · 4 min read

WBCQ The Planet in Monticello, Maine is looking for a new tenant for its 500 kW “Superstation” transmitter on 9330 kHz. The station’s own website lists the transmitter and its fully rotatable antenna as “now available for your lease,” months after the broadcaster that filled 9330 kHz around the clock went off the air.

At a glance
  • What: a 500 kW Continental Electronics transmitter and a rotatable curtain antenna array in Monticello, Maine
  • Frequency: 9330 kHz (31 metre band)
  • Status: advertised for lease on wbcq.com (page dated June 9, 2026). I found no announcement of a sale.
  • Previous tenant: World’s Last Chance (WLC), full time as of 2023, reported off WBCQ in January 2026
  • WBCQ itself: still on the air on its other shortwave transmitters

How we got here

WhenWhat happened
March 2018WBCQ announces a 500 kW Continental Electronics transmitter and a rotatable curtain array from Ampegon. It was built with private investors, reportedly tied to a religious organization (SWLing Post).
20239330 kHz is leased full time to World’s Last Chance, a religious broadcaster (Wikipedia).
January 2026Listeners report that WLC has left WBCQ. Glenn Hauser’s World of Radio forum says WLC is bankrupt. A message on WLC’s own website cited growing financial challenges, suspended projects and a request for donations, without using the word bankruptcy (forum report).
June 9, 2026wbcq.com lists the Monticello Maine Superstation, 9.330 MHz at up to 500 kW with a fully rotatable antenna, as available to lease (WBCQ).

What is confirmed, and what is not

Confirmed: WBCQ is advertising the 500 kW transmitter and antenna for lease, and WLC is no longer broadcasting from it.

Not confirmed:

  • A sale. The listing says lease. Some reports and social posts have said “for sale,” but I could not find that in anything WBCQ has published.
  • The lease terms. One forum poster who contacted WBCQ said it wants long-term leases in 12-hour blocks. That is secondhand, so contact WBCQ directly if you are interested.
  • Who controls the equipment. The forum thread raised the question of who now controls the 500 kW unit. I have not seen an answer.
  • A new tenant. I have not seen one announced. Check wbcq.com for the latest.

What it means for WBCQ

This does not take WBCQ off the air. The lease listing covers the 9330 kHz Superstation only. In the A-26 schedule data, WBCQ The Planet is also filed on 7490 kHz (50 kW, 1600–0400 UTC), 6160 kHz (5 kW, 0000–0100 and 1600–2400 UTC) and 3265 kHz (50 kW, 0000–0100 UTC). Check the station’s own program guide for the current lineup before you tune.

The money side is harder. WBCQ has not said how the loss of a full-time 9330 kHz tenant affects its finances, and I will not guess. Independent U.S. shortwave stations generally rely on selling airtime, so a vacant 500 kW slot matters.

What it means for listeners

A 500 kW signal with an antenna that can be pointed anywhere is a rare tool. The antenna is described as fully rotatable, so a new lessee could aim it at different regions. If one signs on, 9330 kHz could come back aimed at a new region, with a new language and a new format.

Check before you tune. Our schedule data comes from the EIBI and HFCC A-26 files, which still list 9330 kHz as “WBCQ World’s Last Chance” for 24 hours a day at 500 kW (see 9330 kHz). Those files lag real life, so treat that listing as unconfirmed. If you hear something on 9330 kHz, or hear only noise, tell me. The new B-26 season starts October 25, and the season change tracker will show whether 9330 kHz is filed again.

No radio handy? A free WebSDR or KiwiSDR can tell you what is on 9330 kHz right now. Our guide to listening to shortwave radio online shows how.

The bottom line

This is a real loss of airtime for the hobby, and not the end of WBCQ. A 500 kW anchor tenant is gone, and the equipment is available. What happens next depends on whether someone with a message and a budget picks up the lease. I will update this article when there is news.
